verses.en: A long time[NOTE:1] passed after the Lord made Israel secure from all their enemies,[NOTE:2] and Joshua was very old.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “many days.”
Heb “the Lord had given rest to Israel from their enemies all around.”
Heb “was old, coming into the days.” This expression, referring to advancing in years, also occurs in the following verse.

23:1 "after many days" Although it seems from the biblical account that the
conquest of Canaan happened very rapidly, in reality it took a long time. The Canaanites
were not easily or totally defeated (cf. Judges 1). The delay in the last seven tribes' land
allotment is one evidence of the protracted timeframe.

▣ "when the Lord had given rest to Israel from
all their enemies" This is an idiomatic statement. It is a recurrent theme (cf. Deut. 12:10;
25:19; 2 Sam. 7:1,11; 2 Chr. 14:7). It probably means there was no current national military
campaign in progress (cf. Jos. 21:44). It did not apply to the individual tribes possessing
their own allotted territories. The phrase has connotations of

- no war

- security from invasion

- peace

verses.zh: 就把以色列众人的长老、族长、审判官，并官长都召了来，对他们说：「我年纪已经老迈。
verses.en: So Joshua summoned all Israel, including the elders, rulers, judges, and leaders, and told them: “I am very old.
verses.commentary:
23:2 "Joshua called" Chapter 23 seems to have been a private meeting with
the tribal representatives, while chapter 24 is a more public meeting calling for a
public decision.

▣

"elders. . .heads. . .judges. . .officers"

NJB

The exact function of each of these groups is uncertain
(cf. Deut. 1:15-16; Jos. 8:33) but there was a distinct division of leadership on a
tribal level. See fuller note at Jos. 24:1.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们的　神因你们的缘故向那些国所行的一切事，你们亲眼看见了，因那为你们争战的是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: You saw everything the Lord your God did to all these nations on your behalf, for the Lord your God fights for you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for the Lord your God, he [is] the one who fights for you.”
verses.commentary:
23:3 "the Lord your God" This is a technical phrase for
the Covenant relationship. It is used extensively in Deuteronomy and Joshua.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

23:3-4 "to all these nations . . . which remain" It seems that Joshua defeated
the military resistance of the Canaanites, but each tribe had to finish the conquest in its
own inheritance (compare Jos. 11:23-24; 21:43-45 with Jos. 13:1-4; 15:63; 23:5 and Jdg. 2:21,23).

▣ "He who has been fighting for you" This same truth is repeated in Jos. 23:5, 9,
and 10. God as warrior is a common theme of the Pentateuch (e.g., Deut. 1:30; 3:22; 20:4; Exod. 14:14)
and Joshua (e.g., 4:13-15; 10:14,42). Notice, however, the previous phrase which emphasized the
necessary cooperation of Israel ("because of you"). YHWH's covenant with Israel had responsibilities
for both parties.

verses.zh: 我所剪除和所剩下的各国，从约旦河起到日落之处的大海，我已经拈阄分给你们各支派为业。
verses.en: See, I have parceled out to your tribes these remaining nations,[NOTE:1] from the Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea[NOTE:2] in the west, including all the nations I defeated.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I have assigned by lots to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes.”
Heb “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.

Heb “from the Jordan and all the nations which I cut off and the Great Sea [at] the place where the sun sets.” The relationship of the second half of the verse, which mentions nations already conquered, to the first half, which speaks of “remaining nations,” is difficult to understand.
verses.commentary:
23:4 "See" This term (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE) is
often used by YHWH in Deuteronomy. It helps the people recognize what He had done
(cf. Exod. 31:2; Deut. 1:8,21; 2:24,31; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39). Here it is used by Joshua for the
elders to recognize his advanced age and the beginning of a new period in Israel's history
in the Promised Land.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们的　神必将他们从你们面前赶出去，使他们离开你们，你们就必得他们的地为业，正如耶和华―你们的　神所应许的。
verses.en: The Lord your God will drive them out from before you and remove them,[NOTE:1] so you can occupy[NOTE:2] their land as the Lord your God promised[NOTE:3] you.
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “from before you.” This has not been included in the translation because it is redundant in English.
Or “take possession of.”
Heb “said to.”
verses.commentary:
23:5 "He will thrust them out from before you" The VERB (BDB 213,
KB 239, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 6:19; 9:4) is SINGULAR in
form, but with a PLURAL suffix. This seems to imply YHWH's agency through
Israel's instrumentality (divine will and human free will, i.e., Exod. 3:7-8 and 3:10).

▣ "just as the Lord your God promised you" This is a
recurrent theme.

verses.zh: 所以，你们要大大壮胆，谨守遵行写在摩西律法书上的一切话，不可偏离左右。
verses.en: Be very strong! Carefully obey[NOTE:1] all that is written in the law scroll of Moses so you won’t swerve from it to the right or the left,
notes: Heb “Be strong so you can be careful to do.”
verses.commentary:
23:6-11

23:6-8 There is a series of things Israel should do to maintain her relationship with YHWH.

- "be very firm," Jos. 23:6, BDB 304, KB 302, Qal PERFECT with
waw, cf. Jos. 1:6,7,9,18; 10:25; 23:6; Deut. 31:6,7,23

- "to keep," Jos. 23:6, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 4:6; 29:9

- "to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses," Jos. 23:6, BDB 793, KB 889, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Jos. 1:7; Num. 15:39; Deut. 16:12; 30:8

- "you may not turn aside from it," Jos. 23:6, BDB 693, KB 747, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, e.g., using two synonymous VERBS, Jos. 1:7;
Exod. 32:8; Deut. 2:27; 5:32; 9:12; 11:16; 17:17,20; 28:14; 1 Sam. 12:20

- "you will not associate with these nations," Jos. 23:7, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- "do not mention the name of their gods," cf. Exod. 23:13

- "do not make anyone swear by them"

- "do not serve them," cf. Exod. 20:5; 23:33

- "do not bow down to them," cf. Jdg. 2:19

- "you are to cling to the Lord," Jos. 23:8, BDB 179, KB 209,
Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Jos. 22:5; Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 13:4; 30:20;
2 Kgs. 18:6. This is the same VERB used to describe Adam and Eve's
relationship (cf. Gen. 2:24).

verses.zh: 不可与你们中间所剩下的这些国民搀杂。他们的神，你们不可提他的名，不可指着他起誓，也不可事奉、叩拜；
verses.en: or associate with these nations that remain near[NOTE:1] you. You must not invoke or make solemn declarations by the names of their gods![NOTE:2] You must not worship[NOTE:3] or bow down to them!
notes: Heb “with.”

Heb “and in the name of their gods you must not invoke and you must not make solemn declarations.” The words “and you must not make solemn declarations” are omitted in the LXX and may represent a later scribal addition to elucidate the immediately preceding command. The Hiphil of שָׁבַע (shavaʿ) without an object occurs only here and in Josh 6:26.
Or “serve.”

verses.zh: 只要照着你们到今日所行的，专靠耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: But you must be loyal to[NOTE:1] the Lord your God, as you have been[NOTE:2] to this very day.
notes: Heb “hug.”
Heb “done.”

verses.zh: 因为耶和华已经把又大又强的国民从你们面前赶出；直到今日，没有一人在你们面前站立得住。
verses.en: “The Lord drove out from before you great and mighty nations; no one has been able to resist you[NOTE:1] to this very day.
notes: Heb “not a man has stood before you.”
verses.commentary:
23:9 "For the Lord has driven out great and strong nations from before you" The
VERB (BDB 439, KB 441, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw)
is recurrent (e.g., 3:10; 13:6; Num. 33:52,55, used in the sense of "dispossess").

YHWH's ownership of the land is symbolized in His victory over the Canaanites. Yes,
Israel goes to battle, but it is the power and presence of YHWH that brings victory over vastly superior
foes (cf. Deut. 4:38; 9:1; 11:23).

Israel's lack of military success (i.e., they did not dispossess, cf. Jos. 13:13; 16:10;
17:13; Jdg. 1:29,30,31, 32,33) was due to their lack of faith in YHWH's promises and their unwillingness
to seize the moment! The unbelief of the ten original spies returns!

▣ "no man has stood before you to this day" This is imagery for negated effective
resistance (cf. Jos. 1:5; 10:8; Deut. 7:24; 11:25).

verses.zh: 你们一人必追赶千人，因耶和华―你们的　神照他所应许的，为你们争战。
verses.en: One of you makes a thousand run away,[NOTE:1] for the Lord your God fights for you,[NOTE:2] as he promised you he would.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “chases a thousand.”
Heb “for the Lord your God, he [is] the one who fights for you.”
Heb “as he said to you.”
verses.commentary:
23:10 "One of your men puts to flight a thousand" This is hyperbolic expression of
YHWH's victorious presence (cf. Lev. 26:7-8; Deut. 32:30).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 你们要分外谨慎，爱耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Watch yourselves carefully! Love the Lord your God![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Watch carefully yourselves so as to love the Lord your God.”
verses.commentary:
23:11 Loving YHWH is expressed by covenant obedience! Love is an action,
not just a feeling. Believers must make a decisive and personal choice to obey God! This
is a recurrent theme in Deuteronomy (e.g., Deut. 6:5; 10:12; 11:13).

verses.zh: 你们若稍微转去，与你们中间所剩下的这些国民联络，彼此结亲，互相往来，
verses.en: But if you ever turn away and make alliances with[NOTE:1] these nations that remain near you,[NOTE:2] and intermarry with them and establish friendly relations with them,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and hug.”
Heb “the remnant of the these nations, these nations that are with you.”
Heb “and go into them, and they into you.”

- "if you ever go back," BDB 996, KB 1427, both the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and

PERFECT with waw, cf. Jos. 23:7

verses.zh: 你们要确实知道，耶和华―你们的　神必不再将他们从你们眼前赶出；他们却要成为你们的网罗、机槛、肋上的鞭、眼中的刺，直到你们在耶和华―你们　神所赐的这美地上灭亡。
verses.en: know for certain that the Lord your God will no longer drive out these nations from before you. They will trap and ensnare you;[NOTE:1] they will be a whip that tears[NOTE:2] your sides and thorns that blind[NOTE:3] your eyes until you disappear[NOTE:4] from this good land the Lord your God gave you.
notes: Heb “be a trap and a snare to you.”
Heb “in.”
Heb “thorns in your eyes.”
Or “perish.”
verses.commentary:
23:13 "know with certainty" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a
Qal IMPERFECT of the same root (BDB 393, KB 390) for emphasis.

▣ This is a list of the consequences of disobedience to the covenant.

- "The Lord your God will not continue to drive these nations out"

- They will be

- "a snare" (used to catch birds, BDB 809 I, cf. Exod. 23:33; 34:12; Deut. 7:16)

- "a trap" (a trap set on the ground, BDB 430)

- "a whip on your sides" (like an animal goad, BDB 1002)

- "thorns in your eyes" (BDB 841, cf. Num. 33:55; Jdg. 2:3)

cf. Deut. 4:26; 7:4

verses.zh: 「我现在要走世人必走的路。你们是一心一意地知道，耶和华―你们　神所应许赐福与你们的话没有一句落空，都应验在你们身上了。
verses.en: “Look, today I am about to die.[NOTE:1] You know with all your heart and being[NOTE:2] that not even one of all the faithful promises the Lord your God made to you is left unfulfilled; every one was realized—not one promise is unfulfilled![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “go the way of all the earth.”
Or “soul.”
Heb “one word from all these words which the Lord your God spoke to you has not fallen, the whole has come to pass for you, one word from it has not fallen.”

23:14-16

23:14 "I am going the way of all the earth" This is an idiom or euphemism for death
(cf. Gen. 3:19; 1 Kgs. 2:2).

▣ "you know in all your hearts and in all your souls" The VERB
(BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT with waw) reinforced the Israelites'
sense of YHWH's special presence and provisions. He has completely fulfilled all of His promises.

The parallel phrases "in all your hearts" and "in all your souls" are synonymous
and refer to the entire person. Each Israelite knew for sure, completely, without doubt that YHWH
was faithful to His word to them (cf. Jos. 21:45)! They must emulate this same faithfulness
(i.e., Jos. 23:6-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW (using mostly Deuteronomy as a paradigm)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "not one of them has failed" God's promises are sure and
conditional (cf. Jos. 23:15; 21:45; 1 Kgs. 8:56).

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们　神所应许的一切福气怎样临到你们身上，耶和华也必照样使各样祸患临到你们身上，直到把你们从耶和华―你们　神所赐的这美地上除灭。
verses.en: But in the same way that every faithful promise the Lord your God made to you has been realized,[NOTE:1] it is just as certain that if you disobey, then the Lord will bring on you every judgment[NOTE:2] until he destroys you from this good land that the Lord your God gave you.
notes: Heb “and it will be as every good word which the Lord your God spoke to you has come to pass.”
Heb “so the Lord will bring every injurious [or “evil”] word [or “thing”] upon you.”
verses.commentary:
23:15

23:15 As God's promises of blessing are sure, so are God's warnings of the consequences
of covenant disobedience (cf. Deut. 4:23-31). As God removed the Canaanites from the land
(cf. Gen. 15:12-21), if Israel picks up their habits, He will remove them (i.e., Assyrian and
Babylonian exiles).

verses.zh: 你们若违背耶和华―你们　神吩咐你们所守的约，去事奉别神，叩拜他，耶和华的怒气必向你们发作，使你们在他所赐的美地上速速灭亡。」
verses.en: If you violate the covenantal laws of the Lord your God which he commanded you to keep,[NOTE:1] and you follow, worship, and bow down to other gods,[NOTE:2] then the Lord will be very angry with you and you will disappear[NOTE:3] quickly from the good land that he gave to you.”
notes: Heb “when you violate the covenant of the Lord your God which he commanded you.”
Heb “and you walk and serve other gods and bow down to them.”
Or “perish.”

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

23:16 "transgress" The VERB "transgress" (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) means "to pass over." When used of sin, it means "to pass
over a known boundary"—in this case, the Mosaic covenant.

▣ "the anger of the Lord will burn against you" This
VERB (BDB 354, KB 351, Qal PERFECT with waw) is
often used of YHWH's burning anger for covenant violations (cf. Jos. 7:1; Exod. 4:14; 22:24; 32:10;
Num. 11:1,10,33; 12:9; 22:22; 32:10,13; Deut. 6:15; 7:4; 11:17; 29:27; 31:17; Jdg. 2:20; 3:8; 6:39;
2 Sam. 6:7). This is anthropomorphic language. Humans use human vocabulary to describe the
actions and feelings of God. There is always only an analogous sense.
